def transform(grid):
    out=[row[:] for row in grid]
    pts=[(r,c,v) for r,row in enumerate(grid) for c,v in enumerate(row) if v]
    # Each marker projects its own color along the axis toward the other marker,
    # while a perpendicular leg is colored 5; an offset copy marks the endpoint.
    # Infer by grouping each marker pair and making right-angle paths.
    # Demo pairs: colors 1 and 2, or 3 and 1.
    if len(pts)==2:
        (r1,c1,v1),(r2,c2,v2)=pts
        # paint 5 along the coordinate paths associated with the opposite axis
        # pattern: source1's row/column coordinate propagated to near target.
        # For pairs separated diagonally, one 5-line follows source1's column,
        # and the other follows source2's row.
        if r1!=r2 and c1!=c2:
            # Lines extending from first marker along its column toward second row,
            # and from second marker along its row toward first column.
            dc=1 if r2>r1 else -1
            for r in range(r1+dc, r2, dc):
                out[r][c1]=5
            dr=1 if c1>c2 else -1
            for c in range(c2+dr, c1, dr):
                out[r2][c]=5
            # replica/endpoint markers shifted two cells in the two projected dirs
            if c1+ (2 if c2>c1 else -2) in range(len(out[0])):
                out[r1][c1+(2 if c2>c1 else -2)]=v1
            if c2+ (2 if c1>c2 else -2) in range(len(out[0])):
                out[r2][c2+(2 if c1>c2 else -2)]=v2
        return out
    return out

    points=[(r,c,v) for r,row in enumerate(grid) for c,v in enumerate(row) if v]
